verdict.rationale: GitCafe has no native CI runner in the evidence. CI is handled by integrating an external Buildkite service, whose builds appear on the repository's CI tab and as pull request checks. Signed webhooks and personal access tokens let your own infrastructure react to pushes and talk to the API. Self-hosted execution is therefore only achievable through an external CI tool, and the docs never explicitly describe running jobs on your own or private runners. Missing for 10: native or first-party runner support, explicit documentation of self-hosted/private runner registration and management, hands-on corroboration.
